title: Five problems worth solving
lead: Start with the buyer decision that matters to your business.
body:
01

Our expertise is hard to find

Public information does not answer the buyer’s question.↗02

Our brand is described inconsistently

Facts, products and business units blur across sources.↗03

Our content is hard to use

Important answers sit behind technical or editorial barriers.↗04

We cannot measure AI visibility

Mentions, citations and commercial results get mixed together.↗05

The work has no clear owner

SEO, content, technology and approvals move separately.↗
source: Method / proposed engagement design

title: Visibility has to connect to a decision
lead: A useful programme follows the buyer beyond the first answer.
body:

02

03

VISIBILITY SIGNAL

title: One programme, three connected disciplines
lead: These are working definitions. The same page can support all three.
body:
DisciplineWhat I improveWhat we inspect
SEO
Search engine optimisation		Discovery, index eligibility and organic landing-page performance.Crawls, rendered pages, internal links, search data and conversions.
AEO
Answer engine optimisation		How clearly a page resolves a specific question.Direct answers, conditions, supporting evidence and useful next steps.
GEO
Generative engine optimisation		How the business appears and is cited in generated responses.Repeatable prompt panels, cited URLs and verified factual accuracy.
The supplied research uses “AIO” in several ways. This deck uses AEO for answer quality and treats agent integrations as a separate, optional workstream.
source: Framework adapted from supplied research / Google AI guidance [S1]

title: Two cases. Different constraints.
lead: The work is diagnostic: identify the weak point, define the response and specify how to verify it.
body:
CASE A

Korean Bank

Limited discoverable first-party material, weak English coverage and missing markup in sampled pages.

Commercial question
Can a prospective customer resolve eligibility, product conditions and trust questions?

CASE B

Korean Insurance Company

Fragmented properties, content-rendering concerns and stale English entity information.

Commercial question
Can a prospective customer distinguish the provider, understand coverage and reach the right quote journey?

Evidence boundary: the archive contains public-site observations, inferred risks and simulated answer estimates. It does not demonstrate a deployed programme or measured citation uplift.
source: Case A + Case B / April 2026 audit bundle methodology

title: The missing asset was usable public evidence
lead: A recognised business can still leave important customer questions unanswered.
body:
Reported findingDecision it obstructsFirst validation step
Limited coverage in the inspected sitemapsFinding product, support and corporate information.Compare sitemap entries with a crawl and the CMS inventory.
No English site found at the tested pathsUnderstanding eligibility and access in another language.Map the actual audience, service capability and available pages.
No structured data detected in sampled HTMLInterpreting the provider and product consistently.Inspect raw and rendered HTML across representative templates.
Thin entity and product explanationsChecking conditions and distinguishing facts from commentary.Build a claim inventory with approved source references.
A short sitemap is a discovery clue. It is not a count of indexed pages, and it does not prove that the rest of the site is invisible.
source: Case A / Korean Bank · supplied April 2026 audit · reported observations, not a fresh audit / interpretation qualified using [S2]

title: A source page earns its usefulness
lead: The proposed content makes a claim understandable and maintainable.
body:
ILLUSTRATIVE PAGE STRUCTURE

Account eligibility and access

Eligibility depends on residency, identification and the selected product. Check the current requirements before beginning an application.

Who can apply?
Approved eligibility criteria and exceptions.
What is required?
Documents, verification steps and service limitations.
What changes the answer?
Product conditions and effective dates.
Reviewed by product owner · source reference · review date
  1. A direct answerExplain the question before presenting the brand.
  2. Conditions beside the claimKeep limits and exclusions in the same reading path.
  3. Evidence people can inspectLink to the governing product and disclosure sources.
  4. A useful next actionTake eligible visitors to the appropriate application or support route.

title: The content existed across disconnected journeys
lead: The audit raised questions about discovery, rendering and entity clarity.
body:
Reported findingWhy it mattersWhat must be verified
The tested sitemap endpoint returned 404Some discovery paths may be missing.Alternative sitemap locations, internal links and indexed-page coverage.
Template placeholders appeared in fetched HTMLImportant content may depend on rendering.Raw versus rendered content, crawler access and representative URLs.
Corporate and transactional properties were splitThe customer may reach the wrong product or service route.Purpose of each domain, cross-links, duplicates and conversion paths.
English entity material was stale or shallowAnswers may reuse outdated facts or confuse business units.Current first-party facts and actual responses on selected surfaces.
source: Case B / Korean Insurance Company · supplied April 2026 audit · reported observations, not a fresh audit

title: Clear relationships beat a forced domain merger
lead: The proposed architecture preserves useful journeys while clarifying who provides what.
body:
VERIFIED PROVIDER IDENTITY

Korean Insurance Company

Official name · business scope · current contact routes

Corporate information

Governance, company facts and disclosures.

Product information

Coverage, conditions, exclusions and suitability.

Quote journey

Assign each page a purpose and a maintained relationship. Use canonicals for duplicate or near-duplicate pages; keep genuinely different content independently discoverable.
source: Case B / architecture proposal; canonical guidance [S3]

title: A rendering fix starts with a comparison
lead: A framework name alone cannot tell us what a search system can access.
body:
INITIAL RESPONSE / ILLUSTRATIVE
<h1>Product information</h1>
<div id="details">
  {{ coverage.summary }}
</div>

The key condition is absent from the response.

PROPOSED ACCESSIBLE RESPONSE
<h1>Product information</h1>
<p>Approved coverage summary</p>
<a href="/terms/">
  Conditions and exclusions
</a>

Readers and compatible crawlers receive useful text.

01

Compare

Raw HTML, rendered DOM and URL inspection.

02

Pilot

A small set of important pages.

03

Protect

Consistent content, release checks and rollback.

04

Measure

Access, index status and customer experience.
source: Case B / Korean Insurance Company · supplied April 2026 audit · reported observations, not a fresh audit / schematic example, not a captured client response

lead: Language expansion should follow a serviceable audience and a commercial route.

title: Five controls before publishing a claim
lead: One maintained evidence record should feed the page, markup and review process.
body:
ControlRequired fieldWhy it earns its place
IdentityWhich legal entity, product and market?Prevents mixing facts between related businesses.
MeaningClaim, unit, scope and conditions.Prevents a correct number being used in the wrong context.
EvidenceApproved source and effective date.Gives reviewers a clear basis for verification.
OwnershipContent owner, reviewer and refresh trigger.Turns freshness into a responsibility.
ConsistencyVisible page, metadata and applicable markup agree.Reduces contradictory representations of the same information.
A review date changes when content is actually reviewed. Automated date changes alone do not make an old claim current.
source: Derived from both cases / proposed claim governance

title: Technical changes need a business reason
lead: The implementation brief specifies the symptom, test and smallest useful fix.
body:
SymptomValidate firstPotential response
Key page cannot be reachedStatus codes, access rules, CDN and internal links.Repair the relevant access or linking issue.
Important text appears only after scripts runInitial HTML versus rendered content on the target surface.Server-render or statically publish essential content where justified.
Competing URLs carry the same materialDuplicate content, canonicals and redirects.Consolidate duplicates with a tested migration path.
Facts differ across representationsPage copy, feeds, metadata and schema.Update from a governed claim record.
Different languages serve the wrong intentAudience, equivalent pages and service capability.Create useful locale pages and appropriate language relationships.
source: Proposed engineering brief / Google crawl and canonical guidance [S2, S3]

title: A mention is not a citation
lead: Keep each measure precise enough to support a decision.
body:
MeasureOperational definitionUseful interpretation
Brand mention rateValid responses naming the brand ÷ all valid panel responses.Presence in the sampled answers.
Owned-source citation rateValid responses linking an approved owned domain ÷ all valid panel responses.First-party evidence used in the sampled answers.
Verified claim accuracyCorrect, checkable claims ÷ all checkable claims about the brand.Quality of factual representation; record uncheckable claims separately.
Citation share within a defined setOwned-domain citations ÷ citations to all tracked domains.Relative presence for that panel and domain set only.
Qualified action rateQualified enquiries or completed applications ÷ relevant measured visits.Commercial quality of the observable journey.
source: Measurement definitions proposed for this programme; do not compare incompatible denominators

title: A repeatable panel creates a usable baseline
lead: The scope below is a proposed pilot design, not a historical audit result.
body:
40prompts
×
3selected surfaces
×
2repeat runs
=
240attempted responses
STRATIFY

Intent and language

Split branded and unbranded questions. Cover trust, eligibility, comparison and action. Separate language cohorts.

RECORD

The actual conditions

Save exact prompt, date, locale, surface, mode, full answer and linked URLs. Mark refusals, failures and no-answer responses.

COMPARE

Like with like

Use new sessions and fixed settings where possible. Report counts and variation by cohort. Track model or product changes.

A synthetic prompt panel is a diagnostic sample. It is not the market’s query volume, audience reach or total share of demand.
source: Proposed research protocol adapted from the archive prompt kits

title: The dashboard should tell us what to do next
lead: Every signal needs a denominator, a source and a decision.
body:
LayerWhat appears in the reportDecision it supports
DeliveryApproved fixes shipped / committed fixes; ageing blockers.Remove dependencies or narrow scope.
Technical accessPilot URLs accessible / tested; index observations by URL.Repair failed templates or discovery paths.
Answer qualityOwned citations / valid responses; correct / checkable claims.Improve a specific source page or correct a factual gap.
BehaviourObserved referral visits, engaged sessions and qualified actions.Improve the landing page or next-step journey.
Commercial outcomeQualified pipeline or applications with documented attribution.Continue, modify or pause the investment.
Engine dashboards and prompt panels answer different questions. Keep their totals separate; missing referral data does not prove zero influence.
source: Proposed reporting model / Bing aggregated citation reporting [S4]

title: The first quarter builds an operating capability
lead: Dates are indicative and depend on access, approvals and delivery capacity.
body:
DAYS 1–15

Establish the baseline

Agree a product family, buyer intents and access. Revalidate audit signals and run the first panel.

Gate: evidence and scope accepted
DAYS 16–30

Remove critical barriers

Address access or content faults. Approve claim records, release plan and page specifications.

Gate: release-ready backlog
DAYS 31–60

Publish the pilot

Release a bounded page set. Validate content, tracking and relevant technical changes.

Gate: release quality accepted
DAYS 61–90

Review and expand

Rerun the panel. Review qualified actions and blockers. Set the next-quarter investment.

Gate: scale, revise or pause
The commitment is an accountable delivery process with explicit acceptance criteria. Rankings, citations and revenue are outcomes to measure, not guarantee.
source: Proposed roadmap adapted from both case workstreams

title: The mandate is wider than a content calendar
lead: Prospective clients buy a clear owner for a connected business problem.
body:
“We have an SEO agency, content and technology teams.
Who connects the decisions?”

Illustrative buyer situation, not a client quotation.

  1. Translate the commercial problemChoose the buyer journey and the business measure.
  2. Make the work executableTurn audit findings into scoped releases and clear ownership.
  3. Challenge weak evidenceSeparate observed results from assumptions and vendor claims.
  4. Maintain the programmeRefresh facts, monitor changes and reallocate effort.
The fractional role complements specialist execution. It works best when the sponsor supplies access, authority and enough capacity to act.
source: Demand Journeys / proposed value proposition
